title: The Unstable Text
text:
Postmodern novels often refuse to offer a single, stable interpretation. Instead, they foreground their own artifice, inviting readers to notice the seams of the narrative. Authors such as Italo Calvino and Donald Barthelme used fragmentation and self-reference to question the very notion of authorial authority. Readers are thus cast not as passive recipients but as active co-producers of meaning.

Critics have divided over whether this experimental stance is liberating or merely a sophisticated form of detachment. Proponents argue that it democratizes literature by dismantling hierarchies between text and reader. Skeptics counter that irony without commitment can become an evasion of moral responsibility, leaving the reader with clever games but few convictions.

questions.text: According to paragraph one, what do postmodern novels often do instead of offering a single stable interpretation?
options: They end with a clear moral
They avoid using any narrative structure

questions.text: According to paragraph two, what do skeptics argue that irony without commitment can become?
options: A more democratic form of readership

questions.text: What can be inferred about the author's attitude towards postmodern experimentation?
options: It is endorsed without any reservation
It is presented as contested rather than settled
It is dismissed as having no literary value
It is described as a purely commercial trend

questions.text: Why does the passage describe readers as 'active co-producers of meaning'?
options: Because readers must edit books before publication
Because the text is completed by the reader's own interpretation
Because readers write the sequels to postmodern novels

vocabulary.definition: a clever or contrived device that makes a work seem artificial
the breaking of a whole into disconnected pieces
a lack of emotional involvement or commitment
the act of avoiding a difficult responsibility or question

paragraph_translations: Powieści postmodernistyczne często nie chcą zaoferować jednej, stabilnej interpretacji. Zamiast tego eksponują swoją sztuczność, zachęcając czytelników do dostrzeżenia szwów narracji. Autorzy tacy jak Italo Calvino i Donald Barthelme posługiwali się fragmentaryzacją i autotematyzmem, by podważyć samą ideę autorytetu autora. Czytelnicy zostają więc postawieni nie jako bierni odbiorcy, lecz jako aktywni współtwórcy znaczenia.

Krytycy podzielili się co do tego, czy ta eksperymentalna postawa jest wyzwalająca, czy też jest jedynie wyrafinowaną formą dystansu. Zwolennicy twierdzą, że demokratyzuje ona literaturę, burząc hierarchie między tekstem a czytelnikiem. Sceptycy odpowiadają, że ironia pozbawiona zaangażowania może stać się unikiem odpowiedzialności moralnej, pozostawiając czytelnikowi sprytne gry, ale niewiele przekonań.
